turns.customer: First time boarding Coco. What should I bring? Can she eat her own food?
blocks:
Yes—Happy Tails encourages bringing Coco’s **usual food** to help avoid stomach upset. If you forget it, their in-house food is available at the owner’s request for **$3 per day**. ([happytailspetresorttx.com](https://www.happytailspetresorttx.com/services/dog-boarding))

For packing, bring:
- **Her regular food** for the stay.
- If you’d like, **one hard chew toy** at least 2½ inches in diameter. No rawhides, rope toys, or destructible toys.
- **Written proof of required vaccinations and screenings** from your veterinarian; the resort requires this before boarding.

Bedding is provided, so you don’t need to pack that. ([happytailspetresorttx.com](https://www.happytailspetresorttx.com/services/dog-boarding))

turns.customer: Oh, and she had fleas a few weeks ago. Is that a problem?
blocks:
A flea problem a few weeks ago doesn’t necessarily mean Coco can’t board, but I couldn’t find a published Happy Tails policy that says how long after fleas a dog must wait or what treatment they require. I’d confirm directly with the resort before her stay and tell them when she last had fleas and what treatment she received; their number is **(512) 764-6150**. ([happytailspetresorttx.com](https://www.happytailspetresorttx.com/services/dog-boarding?utm_source=openai))

If she has any current signs of fleas, check with your veterinarian about treatment before boarding. Happy Tails requires written proof of the listed vaccinations and screenings before dogs can board. ([happytailspetresorttx.com](https://www.happytailspetresorttx.com/vaccination-requirements-policies))
